chunks: My father narrated, may God be pleased with him, who said: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Musa ibn Ja'far al-Baghdadi, from Abu Abdillah al-Isbahani, from Durost, from someone he mentioned, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Six things in which the servants have no agency: knowledge, ignorance, contentment, anger, sleep, and wakefulness.

key_terms.صُنْعٌ: agency, power, or ability to act/choose

ai.seo_question: What are the six things in human life that are beyond our direct control according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq categorizes these six states as 'laysa lil-'ibad fiha sun' (not in human power), distinguishing between innate physiological processes like sleep and psychological states like anger that, while influenced by choice, are ultimately subject to divine decree. This classification underscores the Shia theological balance between human agency (ikhtiyar) and predestination (jabr), reminding believers that even their capacity for knowledge and contentment is a gift from Allah. It serves as a practical reminder to cultivate gratitude for these involuntary blessings while striving to refine the states one can influence.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 6-13 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Ahmad ibn Idris quoted Muhammad ibn Ahmad, on the authority of Musa ibn Ja’far al-Baghdady, on the authority of Aba Abdullah Al-Isbahany, on the authority of Durost, on the authority of someone, on the authority of someone who quoted on the authority of Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB), “
The following six are out of your control: 1. recognition (of God), 2. ignorance, 3. contentment, 4. anger, 5. sleeping, 6. waking up.”
